title: Ohio Truck Factory Layoffs Put Jobs in Focus Before Election
summary:
Nearly 1,400 people were laid off on Wednesday at what had been the Navistar truck factory in Springfield, Ohio. The layoffs came three days before President Donald Trump's planned Saturday rally at a nearby high school. Their scale was roughly equal to an entire year of job growth in the greater Dayton area.

Kyle Bos, 30, was among the workers who lost their jobs. He has two daughters, with a third due in January. He said five items at the grocery store now cost as much as a full cart once did. This was his description of the pressure rising prices were putting on his family.

Bos is a United Auto Workers member who describes himself as a centrist. He indicated that he had voted for Trump three times, but said he no longer supported the president. The layoffs were one reason he planned to spend the final weeks before the November election canvassing for Democrats. Canvassing means talking with people to seek their votes.

The election will test the support of working-class voters who helped Trump and Republicans win power. In Ohio, Republican Senator Jon Husted faces former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown. Their race could help determine which party controls the Senate.

The Dayton area has lost about half of its 90,000 factory jobs since 1990, according to federal data. More recently, its economy has improved as Wright-Patterson Air Force Base expanded. The base directly employs 38,000 people, and its innovations have attracted aerospace companies, including Electra.

Trump said manufacturing was returning during a visit to a Texas truck plant. The White House cited Electra's $850 million investment and announcements from Honda and Stellantis as evidence that Trump's policies were creating jobs.

Jeff Hoagland, CEO of the Dayton Development Coalition, offered a longer view of the area's growth. He said Republicans and Democrats alike had recognized Wright-Patterson's value over the past two decades. He also explained that economic development takes time.
why_it_matters: The layoffs show how employment and household costs can shape voters' concerns, while the area's recent growth provides context for claims about the economy.
